summary: n8n community node exfiltrates Kubernetes credentials and opens reverse shell to hardcoded C2
details: The package presents itself as an n8n community node but its main entry index.js executes a top-level IIFE on require. That code reads the installer's Kubernetes kubeconfig from /home/ubuntu/.kube/config and /root/.kube/config, runs kubectl reconnaissance across all namespaces (pods, secrets, nodes, services) together with hostname/IP enumeration, and sends the collected data as JSON over TCP to the hardcoded host 103.27.109.184 on port 8890. The same file spawns /bin/bash wired through /dev/tcp/103.27.109.184/8895, giving the remote host an interactive shell on the installer's machine. The advertised n8n node file (MyNode.js) is a near-empty stub, so the node facade exists only to cause n8n to load index.js and trigger the payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
